sessions.phase_name: Phase 8 pre-work - events_created reconciliation mismatch defect fix
sessions.summary: SEPARATE DEFECT from S0013 (routes fix) with a distinct root cause, found during the same diagnostic session; logged as its own entry. Bug: the events_created dashboard count filtered on Event.is_valid.is_(True), Event.is_edit.is_(False), treating created/edited as mutually exclusive; but every valid event was created AND some were later ALSO edited (both immutable facts matching event_created / event_edited receipts). When an FR-2 edit flips is_edit to True the row dropped out of events_created, producing nonzero variance (events_created: dashboard_count=0, receipt_count=1). Not caught by the original suite: no test combined create + edit + reconciliation. Fix: events_created query now filters ONLY on is_valid.is_(True); events_edited unchanged (is_edit monotonic). events_created and events_edited are now intentionally OVERLAPPING (not a partition) - correct model, not a double-count bug.

sessions.summary: DeadLetterQueue model (table dead_letter_queue: id PK, event_id FK, stage, error, retry_count, resolved default false, created_at); Alembic 0010_dead_letter_queue (down_revision 0009). interpret.py: on retry exhaustion (bounded by _is_retryable) the event is dead-lettered - a dead_letter_queue row (stage="interpret", sanitized/truncated error <=500 chars, retry_count=actual attempts) plus a dead_lettered receipt in a SINGLE commit (FR-9 atomicity), replacing the previous interpreted/status=error receipt. Per-attempt backoffs logged via structlog, not receipted. Retry config env-configurable: retry_max_attempts (default 3) and retry_base_delay_ms (default 500) from RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS/RETRY_BASE_DELAY_MS. events.py + schemas/responses.py: exhaustion returns status="dead_letter", stage="interpret"; pipeline halts (confirmed short-circuit already prevented score/act). dashboard.py: added dead_letter_queue reconciliation pair (dead_letter_queue <-> dead_lettered). Finding: "error" is never used as an action_type anywhere (only as a status); retiring error-as-action_type was a no-op; exhaustion receipt uses action_type="dead_lettered", status="error". Decision: dead_letter_queue IS a reconciliation pair (row vs dead_lettered receipt, written atomically 1:1) added deliberately and disclosed.

sessions.summary: Audit of Phases 0-8 against PRD v1.2 and the implementation plan, then fixes for every issue found (6 defects reported + a 7th surfaced while fixing). D1 payload_hash not advanced on edit (ingest.py): the column is the stored comparand for future submissions on the same dedupe_key, so the row stayed permanently unequal to its own content - the edited payload re-detected as an edit forever (extra event_edited receipt + redundant interpret/score/act each time, unbounded reconciliation variance) while the original payload was misread as a duplicate, silently discarding a revert; fix advances the hash and records previous_payload_hash + payload_hash in the receipt metadata. D2 create_new review resolution minted an Identity with no identity_created receipt (FR-9 violation; identities vs identity_created pair permanently nonzero); fix writes the receipt with match_rule=manual_review_resolve, match_confidence=1.00, review_id, plus the structured log line, and derives display_name from the event's identity_fields. D3 resolving a manual review never resumed the pipeline (Flow 3 step 4): ingest halts an ambiguous event before interpret, so resolution is the only thing that can un-halt it, but resolve only linked the identity - the event was left with no interpretation/score/lead/route/touch permanently. Fix extracts app/services/pipeline.py::run_downstream as the single shared interpret->score->act runner and points all three entry points at it (ingest, manual-review resume, admin replay) so they cannot drift; ingest and resume surface exhausted retries as 202 status=dead_letter, replay keeps 503 replay_failed; resolve now returns pipeline_status/label/score/decision_outcome/lead_id/lead_op/queue/rule_matched/sla_deadline/attribution_touch_id per the PRD API table. D4 UNIQUE(events.dedupe_key) was global, not scoped to accepted rows - two symptoms from one cause: (a) resubmitting the same schema-invalid payload raised IntegrityError -> 500, breaking 'never silently drop an invalid event' since the caller got an error instead of a persisted rejection; (b) a corrected resubmission matched the rejected row's dedupe_key and was treated as an EDIT of a row still flagged is_valid=false, running the pipeline against it and never producing a clean accepted event. Fix: migration 0011 replaces the constraint with a partial unique index WHERE is_valid = true AND dedupe_key IS NOT NULL, and find_event_by_dedupe_key is scoped to is_valid = true to match. Considered and rejected: catching IntegrityError in persist_invalid_event and collapsing repeat rejections onto one row - fixes only (a), leaves (b), and desynchronizes the events_rejected vs event_rejected pair (one row, N receipts). The migration looks the auto-generated constraint name up from pg_constraint rather than hardcoding events_dedupe_key_key; downgrade() NULLs duplicate dedupe_keys (keeping the oldest valid row) before restoring the global constraint so no audit row is deleted. D5 routes.escalated was never evaluated - three docstrings described it as computed-on-read but nothing computed it, escalated was absent from the /leads list payload, and FR-9's escalated action type was missing from VALID_ACTION_TYPES so the transition could not have been receipted. Fix: new app/services/escalation.py with a pure is_sla_breached (strict <, so exactly on the deadline is not yet breached, matching the >=-at-threshold convention in resolve.should_auto_link and score._decide; naive timestamps coerced to UTC rather than raising) and evaluate_escalation performing a monotonic false->true transition, writing the escalated receipt once, not committing (caller owns the transaction). On-read detection rather than a scheduler is the PRD's own recommendation (section 12 open item, line 421) - no new dependency. D6 manual_review_queue.resolved_at left NULL on resolution; fixed in the same resolve_review rewrite, both branches now commit exactly once. D7 (found while fixing) events_edited reconciliation manufactured variance: events.is_edit is a sticky boolean so the entity side counts 'ever edited' while the receipt side counted raw event_edited receipts - any twice-edited event reported variance 1 and failed the FR-10 / success-criterion-2 gate. Fixed with COUNT(DISTINCT receipts.event_id) on that pair only; all 8 pairs audited, it is the only one affected. API gaps closed: GET /api/v1/dead-letter (new app/routers/dead_letter.py) - the PRD Error States table promises a dead-lettered event is visible there, but Phase 8b wrote the rows and 8c added replay with nothing able to enumerate what needed replaying without direct SQL; read-only and unauthenticated (PRD lists 200 only; the bearer gate covers the mutating admin endpoints), ?resolved= filtered, oldest-first because the list doubles as a replay worklist, each entry carrying a replay_url. /dashboard/reconciliation now returns the PRD's top-level {variance, status: PASS|FAIL} alongside the FR-10 per-metric rows and accepts since/until applied to BOTH sides of every comparison - exact because Postgres evaluates now() once per transaction and an entity plus its receipt are written in one transaction, so a window cannot split a pair; overall_status and total_variance retained as aliases. Deliberately NOT added: interpreted/scored reconciliation pairs, since those receipts accumulate per re-run while the row count stays at 1 (interpretations.event_id is UNIQUE), which would break the variance-0 gate by construction. Compliance (Phase 1 / Phase 3 gates): README.md now carries the LIVE/SIMULATED/TEST/MOCKED table at the point of use - all three connectors SIMULATED (internal fixture generators, no Reddit/social/ESP API ever called), classification LIVE via OpenRouter, simulate-failure test-harness-only, test-suite LLM calls MOCKED - plus the two efficiency short-circuits that mean not every event triggers the LIVE call, and a migration note for 0011. Out of scope on purpose: /api/v1/dashboard/summary and the Jinja2 dashboard screens are Phase 9 per the implementation plan.

sessions.phase: Defect - Edit of dead-lettered event returns 500 instead of 202 (regression from Follow-up B, live testing catch)
sessions.phase_name: Defect - Edit of dead-lettered event returns 500 instead of 202 (regression from Follow-up B, live testing catch)
sessions.summary: Defect found during live end-to-end testing (edit of a dead-lettered event), not caught by test suite — regression introduced by Follow-up B (Fix-10 DB constraint). Bug: Follow-up B added partial unique index uq_dead_letter_queue_event_id_unresolved and duplicate_suppressed branch in classify_event that correctly re-raised InterpretError, but the event ORM object becomes expired after await db.rollback() inside that branch. Caller in app/routers/events.py:154 then did str(event.id) after await run_downstream raised, triggering lazy load outside greenlet (MissingGreenlet), which is not InterpretError, so except InterpretError did not catch it and it propagated as 500. Why not caught: suite builds schema via Base.metadata.create_all (bypasses alembic_version) and no test ever did dead-letter -> edit of same external_event_id while provider still failing; existing dead-letter tests use distinct IDs and the replay re-dead-letter test goes through admin.py which does not access event.id after the error. Fix: capture event_id_str = str(event.id) before await run_downstream in events.py and use it in the except dead-letter response; interpret.py duplicate branch already correctly re-raises InterpretError identically to normal path (verified). Also verified manual_review.py and admin.py are not affected (they use resolved["event_id"] or no event.id). Regression: tests/integration/test_fix_deadletter_edit_regression.py (1 test) fails before (MissingGreenlet 500) and passes after (202 dead_letter).
sessions.verification: Before fix: test_edit_of_dead_lettered_event_still_returns_202_not_500 -> FAILED MissingGreenlet (500). After fix: 1 passed; full suite 242 passed 1 skipped (was 241, +1 new). Verified duplicate_suppressed branch still raises InterpretError identically (git show). Code trace confirms only ingest edit path was affected.
prompts_or_hashes: Real bug found during live end-to-end testing (not caught by the test suite). Reproduction: submit an event with real text while OPENROUTER_API_KEY is invalid/expired, so it dead-letters. Then submit an EDIT of that same event (same external_event_id, different payload). Expected: same 202 dead_letter response. Actual: raw 500 Internal Server Error, unhandled exception.

sessions.phase_name: Defect - Fresh-clone startup fails on empty int env vars (ValidationError on cp .env.example .env)
sessions.summary: Defect found during genuine clean-environment verification (cp .env.example .env + only ADMIN_API_KEY), not caught by suite. Bug: .env.example shipped RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS=, RETRY_BASE_DELAY_MS=, INTERPRET_MIN_TOKENS= as empty (names-only). On fresh clone cp .env.example .env + only ADMIN_API_KEY, those stay "" which pydantic-settings presents as "" for int fields -> ValidationError int_parsing at Settings() startup (before ADMIN_API_KEY check). docker-compose already had ${VAR:-default} so docker compose config looked OK, masking host Settings() failure. No prior test exercised Settings() with "" for those ints. Fix: app/config.py added field_validator mode=before for those three ints that treats ""/None as missing -> Field default (2/3/500), parity with docker-compose ${VAR:-default}; .env.example set RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3 RETRY_BASE_DELAY_MS=500 INTERPRET_MIN_TOKENS=2 so fresh .env already valid, validator remains safety net. Verification: before fresh clone Settings() -> ValidationError 3 errors; after -> 2 3 500, docker compose config OK, LLM_PROVIDER=groq blank still succeeds at startup and fails only at get_client() mirroring openrouter.
sessions.verification: Before: fresh clone without validator ADMIN_API_KEY=test python3 -c 'from app.config import Settings; Settings()' -> ValidationError 3 int_parsing input_value='' . After: git clone file://$(pwd) /tmp/dsw-fresh && cp .env.example .env && printf ADMIN_API_KEY=... >>.env -> python3 -c Settings() prints 2 3 500; docker compose config OK; LLM_PROVIDER=groq GROQ_API_KEY='' succeeds at startup, fails only at get_client() RuntimeError GROQ_API_KEY not configured (mirroring OPENROUTER). pytest -q still 249 passed 1 skipped.
